brief: SEB expects the Fed to hold its policy rate at 3.50-3.75% at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting, but calls it a very close call: the 11 September CPI print is the single data point that decides it. SEB forecasts y/y core CPI decelerating from 2.5% to 2.4%, which it believes is enough to keep the Fed on hold, though the details feeding the Fed's preferred core PCE gauge matter too. Markets shifted to pricing 50/50 odds for a hike after Waller's speech, then to 60% after a stronger-than-expected August payrolls report, though SEB does not think Fed members will weight the strong jobs data heavily. Three regional presidents (Hammack, Logan, Kashkari) already voted to hike in July; several Governing Board members (Cook, Williams, Barr, Waller) have signaled openness to holding if inflation data cooperates. Chair Warsh sharpened his hawkish inflation credentials at Jackson Hole, but SEB does not read that as a signal for September, given his opposition to forward guidance. SEB continues to forecast that rates have peaked, though it has pushed expected cuts to September 2027 and March 2028, with risks skewed to the upside from limited Fed tolerance for inflation setbacks and renewed Middle East oil-price pressure.
